name: Munjr Subscriptions with Recurly for WooCommerce
author: munjr

sections.description:
Munjr Subscriptions with Recurly for WooCommerce connects a WooCommerce store to Recurly. You sell the subscription in WooCommerce. Recurly creates the plan, collects the card, and sends the renewal invoices. When a renewal is paid, this plugin creates a WooCommerce order so the shop can fulfill it.

No Munjr license key is required. You use the private API key from your own Recurly account.

  • Connect Recurly from WooCommerce → Settings → Recurly and verify the key in one step.
  • Sell a Recurly Subscription product. Saving it creates the plan in Recurly.
  • Take payment with Recurly.js on classic checkout and on the WooCommerce checkout block. The card number is tokenized by Recurly and is not stored on your site.
  • Show a free-trial badge on the shop and product page, and a $0 trial line in the cart.
  • Bill WooCommerce shipping and tax with the subscription, on the first invoice and on each renewal.
  • Let a logged-in customer cancel at the end of the period, or reactivate, from My Account → Manage Subscriptions.

Requires WooCommerce 8.0 or higher.

This plugin is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Recurly, Inc. or WooCommerce. Recurly is a trademark of Recurly, Inc. WooCommerce is a trademark of Automattic Inc.

Connect your Recurly site

  1. In Recurly, open Integrations → API Credentials and copy the private key for the site you want to bill (production or sandbox).
  2. In WordPress, open WooCommerce → Settings → Recurly.
  3. Paste the key, choose US or EU to match your Recurly data center, and click Verify Connection.
  4. The screen shows the site mode Recurly reports (Production, Sandbox, or Development) and the currencies WooCommerce and Recurly share. Checkout is available only in a shared currency.
  5. Open WooCommerce → Settings → Payments and enable Recurly. The gateway is offered when the cart contains a Recurly subscription.

Create a subscription product

  1. Edit a product and set the product type to Recurly Subscription.
  2. Open the Subscription Plan Config tab.
  3. Set the term length, the recurring price, and the billing period (monthly, every 3 months, every 6 months, yearly, or a custom interval).
  4. Optionally add a trial. Trial length is in days or months. “Trial requires billing info” asks for a card before a $0 trial starts.
  5. Publish the product. Recurly creates a plan with the code wc-{product id}.

On this edition the plan fields lock after that plan exists. Change the plan in Recurly, then use Sync from Recurly to refresh the WooCommerce copy. Editing the plan in both places, and applying a new price to live subscriptions, is part of Recurly Integration Pro.

Checkout

The Recurly payment method appears when the cart needs it. Recurly.js draws the card fields in the shopper’s browser. WordPress receives a token, then creates the Recurly account and the subscription.

A logged-in customer uses the account code wc-user-{id}, so later orders stay on the same Recurly account. A guest always gets a new wc-guest-{order id} account. A guest is not attached to another customer, even when the email matches.

WooCommerce coupons cannot discount a cart that contains a Recurly subscription. A shopper who buys while a WooCommerce sale is running renews at that sale price. This edition does not change the renewal price of people who already subscribed.

A subscription and a one-time product cannot share a cart. The cart and checkout explain that, and checkout stays closed until the cart is only subscriptions or only one-time products.

Trials

When the plan has a trial, the shop and product page show a “Free 14 days trial” style badge on classic templates. The cart line is $0 and names the trial. Recurly still applies the trial on the subscription.

If the trial requires billing info, checkout asks for a card and does not mark the order paid until that step succeeds. If the plan allows a trial without a card, checkout says so and still creates the subscription.

Shipping, tax, and quantity

WooCommerce calculates shipping and tax. Recurly does not recalculate them.

A quantity of 2 or more is one Recurly subscription. The invoice shows that quantity. The plan price is the unit price multiplied by the quantity. The WooCommerce order keeps the same quantity and the same line total.

A virtual subscription has no shipping. For a physical subscription, shipping, tax on the subscription, and tax on shipping are separate billable add-ons. Each uses the subscription quantity when the amount divides into even cents. When the tax does not divide evenly, Recurly is sent the WooCommerce tax total.

Turn on Shipping in Recurly under Configuration → Shipping. The plugin creates a matching shipping method. The fee itself is a billable add-on. If Shipping is off, checkout still charges that add-on instead of failing the order.

On a trial, Recurly would print those add-ons on the trial invoice at $0, including tax, labeled “Trial period for …”. That $0 tax line is the recurring tax add-on, not a second charge for the trial. This plugin does not attach those add-ons when it creates a trial subscription. It schedules them for the next bill date. Shipping and shipping tax that are due today are purchase line items on the signup invoice. A renewal shows the shipping add-on plus a tax line for the subscription and a tax line for shipping. With no trial, the add-ons are charged on the first invoice.

If scheduling the renewal add-ons fails after Recurly has already charged the signup, checkout still completes and the order keeps the subscription. Placing the order again does not create a second subscription or a second charge. A later attempt sends only the subscription change.

Renewals

Copy the webhook URL from WooCommerce → Settings → Recurly → Webhooks into a Recurly endpoint, and enable the renewed subscription notification. You can send a test webhook from that screen. Receipts are listed under WooCommerce → Status → Logs (recurly-webhooks).

A paid renewal invoice creates one WooCommerce order. The same invoice does not create a second order. A failed payment does not create an order. A physical renewal stays Processing so it can be shipped. A virtual renewal is Completed. Plan-change notifications are ignored.

What stays in Recurly

Immediate cancellation, closing a Recurly account, refunds, dunning, and payment retries stay in the Recurly admin. Billing-date changes stay there too. My Account in WooCommerce covers cancel at period end and reactivate.

External services

This plugin connects to Recurly in order to create plans, accounts, and subscriptions, and to collect card details.

Recurly API (https://recurly.com/)

When a store manager saves a Recurly API key, verifies the connection, reloads currencies, saves a subscription product, or when a customer checks out or manages a subscription, the plugin sends requests to the Recurly API for the site configured by that API key. Data sent can include the API key, product and plan fields (name, price, billing interval, trial), order billing details (name, email, address), the WooCommerce customer or guest account code, and a Recurly.js payment token. Card numbers are not sent to the WordPress site.

  • Terms of service: https://recurly.com/legal/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://recurly.com/legal/privacy/

Recurly.js (https://js.recurly.com/v4/recurly.js)

On checkout, when the cart needs a Recurly payment method, the plugin loads Recurly.js from Recurly’s servers. The shopper’s card data is entered in those fields and tokenized by Recurly. The token, not the card number, is posted back to WooCommerce.

  • Terms of service: https://recurly.com/legal/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://recurly.com/legal/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/munjr-subscriptions-with-recurly-for-woocommerce, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate Munjr Subscriptions with Recurly for WooCommerce through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Recurly, enter your Recurly private API key, and use Verify Connection.
  4. Enable the Recurly gateway under WooCommerce → Settings → Payments.
  5. If the My Account subscriptions URL returns 404 after install or upgrade, open Settings → Permalinks and click Save once.
sections.faq:
Does this replace WooCommerce Subscriptions?

No. This integration uses Recurly as the subscription system of record and WooCommerce for catalog and checkout.

Where do I get an API key?

In the Recurly admin under Integrations → API Credentials. Use the private key for the site (production or sandbox) you want WooCommerce to bill.

Do I need a license key?

No. Install and activate the plugin, then connect your own Recurly account.

Can I sell a subscription and a one-time product in the same cart?

No. Mixed carts are blocked at checkout. One-time products and Recurly subscription products need separate orders.

What happens when the quantity is 2 or more?

That quantity is one Recurly subscription. The Recurly invoice shows the quantity, and the plan price is the unit price multiplied by it. The WooCommerce order keeps the same quantity and line total. Shipping and tax are the amounts WooCommerce calculated for that quantity. When the tax does not divide into even cents per unit, Recurly is sent the WooCommerce tax total.

Can I sell a physical subscription?

Yes. WooCommerce calculates shipping and tax, and Recurly bills those amounts with the plan. See “Shipping, tax, and quantity” above for how a trial, a renewal, and a quantity above 1 are sent.

Can customers cancel from their account?

Yes. My Account → Manage Subscriptions lists the customer’s Recurly subscriptions. Cancel stops renewal at the end of the current period. Reactivate undoes that cancellation. Ending a subscription immediately, or refunding an invoice, is done in the Recurly admin.

Does a plan get a price in every WooPayments currency?

No. The plan is priced in the one currency saved when it is created. Checkout in another currency, including a WooPayments currency, is refused.
sections.changelog:
1.2.4

  • A shopper who buys during a WooCommerce sale renews at that sale price. People who already subscribed are not repriced. This edition does not push later plan edits to Recurly.

1.2.3

  • Settings and cache names use the rci_free prefix. Existing values are copied, so the store does not have to reconnect.

1.2.2

  • Admin JavaScript is loaded with WordPress enqueue functions.
  • Classes, functions, and hooks use the rci_free prefix. Stored settings keys are unchanged.

1.2.1

  • If loading the new subscription fails after Recurly has charged the signup, checkout still completes. The order keeps that subscription. Placing the order again does not create a second subscription or a second charge.

1.2.0

  • A paid Recurly renewal creates a WooCommerce order. A physical renewal stays Processing. A virtual renewal is Completed. The same invoice does not create a second order. A failed renewal payment does not create an order.
  • WooCommerce → Settings → Recurly → Webhooks shows the URL to paste into Recurly, can send a test webhook, and logs receipts under WooCommerce → Status → Logs (recurly-webhooks).
  • Plan details stay locked after the Recurly plan is created. Two-way plan sync is not part of this edition.

1.1.7

  • The public name is Munjr Subscriptions with Recurly for WooCommerce. Recurly and WooCommerce come after “with” and “for”. The directory slug is munjr-subscriptions-with-recurly-for-woocommerce. The payment gateway id and the subscription product type are unchanged.
  • The connection warning stays on product and WooCommerce screens. It no longer appears on the main WordPress dashboard.
  • The Recurly PHP client is updated to 4.81.0.

1.1.6

  • If scheduling renewal shipping and tax fails after Recurly has charged the signup, checkout still completes. The order stores the subscription. Placing the order again does not create a second subscription or a second charge. A later attempt sends only that subscription change.

1.1.5

  • A quantity of 2 or more is one Recurly subscription. The invoice quantity matches the WooCommerce quantity, and the price is the unit price multiplied by that quantity. The WooCommerce order keeps that quantity and total.
  • Shipping, subscription tax, and shipping tax are separate add-ons at the subscription quantity. Recurly would list each of those add-ons on a trial invoice as “Trial period for …” at $0, including tax. That $0 tax line is the recurring tax add-on. The add-ons are scheduled for the next bill date, and the signup invoice charges shipping and shipping tax as purchase line items. A renewal shows shipping plus a tax line for the subscription and a tax line for shipping.

1.1.4

  • When the store taxes shipping, a free trial collects that tax on the signup invoice. WooCommerce calculates it. The plugin sends it as a line item on the Recurly purchase that creates the subscription.
  • Each physical subscription in one order is billed its own shipping fee and its own shipping tax.

1.1.3

  • Each subscription in a cart is billed its own tax. Each physical subscription is billed its own shipping. A virtual subscription has no shipping line.
  • A free trial with shipping due today asks for a card and does not mark the order paid or create a subscription until that charge succeeds.

1.1.2

  • The public name is Munjr Recurly Integration for WooCommerce. WordPress.org does not allow a plugin name or slug to start with another company’s trademark, and this plugin is not an official Recurly product. The directory slug is munjr-recurly-integration-for-woocommerce. The payment gateway id and the subscription product type are unchanged.
  • The directory readme records the tested WordPress version as 7.1, which is the format the plugin directory requires. That value is only in this readme, not in the plugin header.

1.1.1

  • When one subscription in an order fails, Recurly is billed the tax for the subscription that succeeds, plus shipping. Tax from the failed line is not charged.

1.1.0

  • Recurly bills the WooCommerce sale price, not the regular plan price.
  • Shipping and tax are billed on the first subscription Recurly accepts, including when an earlier subscription in the order fails.
  • After a free trial, renewal invoices include WooCommerce tax on the plan price.
  • A free trial that does not require a card still creates the Recurly subscription.
  • A guest checkout always gets a new Recurly account, even when the email matches an earlier guest.

1.0.4

  • Recurly charges the WooCommerce shipping amount and tax with the subscription, on the first invoice and on each renewal.
  • The settings screen states that a guest checkout is not attached to a registered customer’s Recurly account.
  • The settings screen states that a later renewal does not create a WooCommerce fulfillment order.

1.0.3

  • Subscription carts can only be paid with Recurly.
  • A guest checkout no longer attaches to a registered customer’s Recurly account.
  • Unchecking Auto renew is saved on the Recurly plan.
  • Uninstall deletes the API key and other plugin options.
  • Checkout errors and My Account subscription statuses can be translated.
  • Loading a subscription product no longer creates a dynamic property on PHP 8.2+.
  • Checkout is blocked when the active currency is not the plan currency.
  • WooCommerce currencies fall back to the store currency when no payment integration reports a currency.

1.0.2

  • The trial badge stays in normal flow under the product title instead of covering the breadcrumb.

1.0.1

  • Unchecking “Trial requires billing info” stays off.
  • Coupons cannot discount a Recurly subscription cart on current WooCommerce.
  • A partial subscription checkout charges only the quantity that succeeded.
  • Mixed carts disable the block cart checkout button.
  • The trial badge no longer covers the product title on block themes.

1.0.0

  • Initial WordPress.org release.
  • Recurly API connection, subscription products, Recurly.js checkout, trials, and My Account subscription management.
  • No license key is required.
